body:
### Description of the problem:

When running a test, bazel uses:
```sh
env - KEY=VALUE ... external/bazel_tools/tools/test/test-setup.sh test+parameters
```

to run the test.  `test-setup.sh` does set `HOME` but does not export it:

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/5b956632c436492545a5be5b13765700b8a01b5f/tools/test/test-setup.sh#L66
  
And so the tests run without `HOME` set.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

<details>
<summary>WORKSPACE</summary>

```
workspace(name = "home")

load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_file")
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

http_archive(
    name = "io_bazel_rules_go",
    urls = [
        "https://storage.googleapis.com/bazel-mirror/github.com/bazelbuild/rules_go/releases/download/v0.21.0/rules_go-v0.21.0.tar.gz",
        "https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_go/releases/download/v0.21.0/rules_go-v0.21.0.tar.gz",
    ],
    sha256 = "b27e55d2dcc9e6020e17614ae6e0374818a3e3ce6f2024036e688ada24110444",
)

load("@io_bazel_rules_go//go:deps.bzl", "go_rules_dependencies", "go_register_toolchains")
go_rules_dependencies()
go_register_toolchains()
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>BUILD</summary>

``` 
load("@io_bazel_rules_go//go:def.bzl", "go_library", "go_test")

go_test(
    name = "acceptance_test",
    srcs = ["acceptance_test.go"],
)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>acceptance_test.go</summary>

```go
package acceptance

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

func TestAcceptance(t *testing.T) {
	if home, found := os.LookupEnv("HOME"); !found {
		t.Error("HOME is not defined")
	} else if home == "" {
		t.Error("HOME is empty")
	} else {
		t.Logf("HOME is %s", home)
	}
}
```

</details>

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

release 2.0.0

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

Surprisingly no!
